title: Lightweight SLO governance, lift plan & QA checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, cross-functional companion for shipping SLOs and simple governance that small product squads can follow without heavy process overhead. It combines a short lift plan, QA checklist for canaries, and a practical governance pattern for SRE and product partners.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- We repeatedly see small services either: (a) ship SLOs that are too strict and trigger noisy paging, or (b) avoid SLOs entirely because the process looks heavy.
- Need a minimal, repeatable pattern to get predictable availability guarantees, clear owner signals, and safe rollout without blocking feature velocity.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus: model-serving endpoints, feature request proxies (API gateway), and latency-sensitive middleware used by hosted API and dedicated deployments.
- Not in scope: long-running batch jobs, infra-only daemons (those follow platform SRE runbooks).

Principles (keep it light):
- 1-page SLO per feature/service. If it fits on a Confluence blurb + a dashboard, it’s good.
- Use 2–3 signals max (latency p50/p95 and request error rate or client-side error rate).
- Start loose, tighten with evidence. Use error budget experiments to validate.
- Prefer automated alerts that escalate to Slack + ticket before paging unless error budget burning is severe.

Quick lift plan (8 working days; intended for small squad + SRE partner):
Day 0: Kickoff: 30m sync, pick SLO owner (product/feature lead) and SRE reviewer. Create ticket (JIRA-XXXX).
Day 1: Draft SLO statement + success criteria. Example: "99.7% of API calls return 200 or 2xx within 200ms p95 per 1h window".
Day 2: Identify telemetry events and dashboard team (Observability). Instrument missing metrics (basic timers/counters).
Day 3: Create dashboard skeleton in Console (latency, count, errors, error-budget burn).
Day 4: Define alerting thresholds (warning at 30% burn/day, page at 60% burn in 1h).
Day 5: Canary rollout plan & QA checklist; rehearse failure injection locally or staging.
Day 6: Canary deploy 10% traffic for 2h. Monitor dashboard and runbook checklist.
Day 7: Canary review, adjust thresholds, update runbook with specific remediation steps.
Day 8: Full rollout and short retrospective (what we learned, owners).

RACI (compressed, as bullets):
- Responsible: Feature owner (sets SLO, signs off instrumentation), SRE reviewer (validates correctness).
- Accountable: Product engineering manager owns final decision to ship SLO.
- Consulted: Observability team (metric names, dashboard), QA (test scenarios).
- Informed: Oncall rotation, support (CS) for customer comms.

Minimal SLO template (one-liner + context):
- Title: short service + signal (e.g., "embed-service latency p95 200ms")
- SLO statement: "Over a rolling 30d window, 99.5% of requests should have p95 latency <= 200ms."
- Signals: metric_name_latency_p95, metric_name_2xx_ratio, request_volume
- Data window: 30d rolling (we use 30d default for product-facing features; infra can use 7d)
- Error budget policy: 1) If burn hits 30%/day -> create ops-ticket and paired pager-lite (Slack + ticket escalation). 2) If burn hits 60% in 1h -> page primary oncall.
- Owner: name + backup oncall alias

Canary & QA checklist (practical, bite-sized):
- Preconditions: CI green, infra capacity checks, smoke tests pass.
- Metric sanity: Ensure latency and error metrics are populated for staging traffic for 24h.
- Synthetic test: run 3 synthetic scenarios (normal, burst, error-rate spike) and capture dashboard.
- Failure injection: simulate an upstream 500 + increased latency for 5m, verify SLO metrics reflect it and runbook steps trigger correctly.
- Backfill checks: confirm there are no gaps in metric ingestion for the last 48h.
- Canary duration & traffic: 2–6h at 5–15% traffic depending on feature blast radius.
- Rollback criteria: if p95 increases > 2x baseline AND error-rate > 1% absolute for 10m -> rollback or throttle.

Lightweight governance pattern (for teams that resist heavy comms):
- Monthly SLO health email (auto-generated) to the squad + stakeholders; keep it 3 bullets: trend, current burn, action needed.
- Quarterly SLO review: 20m demo at squad retro + 10m SRE feedback.
- Exception flow: to change an SLO (tighten/loosen) submit a one-paragraph justification and link to data. SRE reviewer has 3 business days to respond.

Runbook starter (fill-in fields):
- Trigger: exact alert name / condition (e.g., slo-latency-p95-warning)
- Immediate steps: check recent deploys -> check infra capacity -> check upstream errors -> switch to lower-cost variant / degrade non-essential features
- Escalation: create ticket JIRA-XXXX, notify #sre-ops and ping oncall-primary
- Recovery validation: synthetic check passes for 30m, error budget stop burning for 60m
- Postmortem cadence: if page fired, 72h postmortem; if just warning, retro note.

Telemetry and dashboards (obs team notes):
- Required series: request_count, success_count, error_count (4xx/5xx), latency_p50/p95/p99, downstream_latency, queue_length
- Cardinality: prefer aggregated series by route + environment; avoid high-cardinality labels by default. If you need per-customer, open a request with Observability.
- Dashboard templates: use the "SLO-mini" template in Console (deck link above).

Decision heuristics for fallback & graceful degradation:
- If upstream dependency hits 2xx ratio < 95% and retrying increases p95 by > 25%, switch to cached / degraded mode.
- Use feature flags for graceful degradation; default to safe-fail closed behavior for user-facing flows.

Operational play examples (short):
- Example 1: Model-serving memory leak -> symptom: p95 latency rising and error budget burn; immediate action: route new requests to a healthy pool, scale out nonstateful workers, open bug ticket.
- Example 2: Region outage -> detect via region-specific error spike; action: route to fallback region with lower-cost model variant and notify customers on status page.

Open questions & follow-ups (we should discuss at next SLO office hours):
- Should we standardize default canary durations per product line? (proposal: 4h for user-facing, 2h for internal infra)
- What’s the minimal synthetic coverage we require per feature? (proposal: 3 scenarios)
- Define a shared glossary: "page vs ticket vs warning" thresholds across teams.

Next steps (action list):
- Aisha: create JIRA-XXXX and link SLO template (today).
- Mateo: add SLO-mini dashboard template to Console and document metric names (2 days).
- Mei: draft runbook fill-in and put a runbook stub in the repo (3 days).
- Daniel: schedule canary experiment for the next feature launch and invite SRE (this week).

Notes to self / scratch fragments:
- Keep thresholds soft for first 30 days.
- Avoid per-customer paging; prefer aggregated alerting + targeted customer comms from CS.

References:
- Confluence SLO template (link above), Observability dashboard primer, example PR for instrumentation (PR:1812).
